name: International Wire Transfer (Corporate)
orchestration_notes: Corporate Client (PER-002) initiates an international wire via the corporate banking portal (SVC-017). The channel calls SVC-010 (International Payments, CAP-003) synchronously to create an InternationalTransfer record. All cross-capability coordination — account debit (SVC-005, CAP-002), sanctions screening (SVC-051, CAP-005), fraud scoring (SVC-013, CAP-004) — is event-driven via SVC-102 (event bus). SVC-010 may call SVC-009 (Domestic Payments) directly for nostro-leg settlement as a same-capability (CAP-003) synchronous call.
sca_method: FIDO2/WebAuthn biometric or TOTP — PSD2/PSRs 2017. Dynamic linking must bind to beneficiary IBAN/BIC, amount, and currency. Dual authorisation may apply if transfer amount exceeds BusinessAccount.payment_approval_threshold.

phases.name: Transfer Initiation
phases.description: PER-002 accesses the Payments section of the corporate banking portal, enters beneficiary details (name, IBAN, BIC), transfer amount, currency, and a SWIFT purpose code. SCA is completed. SVC-010 validates the BusinessAccount status, available balance, daily limit, and BIC format, then creates an InternationalTransfer record with status = pending_compliance. EVT-049 (InternationalTransferInitiated) is published.
persona_actions: Log in to corporate banking portal (CH-003) or submit via host-to-host API (CH-004)
Enter beneficiary name, beneficiary IBAN, beneficiary BIC (SWIFT code), transfer amount, currency, and ISO 20022 purpose code
Review beneficiary details — including any BIC validation warning if the BIC is not in the SWIFT BIC directory
Select charges type: OUR (all charges borne by sender), SHA (shared), or BEN (beneficiary pays all)
If transfer exceeds BusinessAccount.payment_approval_threshold: second authorised user completes dual authorisation
Complete SCA (FIDO2 biometric or TOTP) with dynamic linking to beneficiary IBAN, amount, and currency
system_actions: SVC-017
SVC-010 validates: BusinessAccount.status = active; available balance >= gbp_equivalent (estimated); BIC in SWIFT BIC directory; purpose code valid per SWIFT code set; amount within daily limit
SVC-010 sets InternationalTransfer.status = pending_compliance
SVC-010 publishes InternationalTransferInitiated (EVT-049) to topic payments.international
phases.exit_condition: InternationalTransfer created with status = pending_compliance; EVT-049 published
nfr_references: SCA completion < 30 seconds customer action budget

phases.name: FX Quotation
phases.description: If the transfer currency differs from the account currency (GBP), SVC-010 obtains an FX rate from the bank's FX pricing engine. For amounts below a threshold (e.g. < £1M equivalent), an indicative rate is applied automatically. For large-value transfers, a firm executable quote is obtained and presented to the customer for acceptance. SVC-010 creates an FXQuotation record (ENT-027) and publishes FXQuoteProvided (EVT-050). The customer has a fixed acceptance window (validity_seconds) before the quote lapses.
persona_actions: View the FX rate, all-in cost, and GBP equivalent displayed by the portal
Accept the FX quote within the validity window (typically 30–120 seconds for firm quotes)
If the quote lapses before acceptance: SVC-010 requests a refreshed quote automatically
system_actions: SVC-010 consumes EVT-049; detects cross-currency requirement (transfer.currency != GBP)
SVC-010 calls internal FX pricing engine (synchronous, intra-capability) to obtain indicative or firm FX rate
SVC-010 creates FXQuotation (ENT-027) with sell_currency = GBP, buy_currency = transfer.currency, rate, validity_seconds, status = pending_acceptance
SVC-010 updates InternationalTransfer.fx_rate and InternationalTransfer.gbp_equivalent
SVC-010 publishes FXQuoteProvided (EVT-050)
On customer acceptance within validity window: FXQuotation.status = accepted; transfer continues to PH-031
On quote lapse: FXQuotation.status = lapsed; SVC-010 requests a new quote automatically and republishes EVT-050
GBP-denominated transfers: PH-030 is skipped; FXQuotation is not created; InternationalTransfer.fx_rate = 1.0000
phases.exit_condition: FXQuotation accepted (or phase skipped for GBP transfers); InternationalTransfer.gbp_equivalent set; EVT-050 published
nfr_references: Firm quote validity window: minimum 30 seconds

phases.name: Pre-Execution Compliance
phases.description: Three compliance checks run concurrently after FX acceptance (or immediately after PH-029 for GBP transfers): (1) sanctions screening of the beneficiary and all intermediary/correspondent banks in the routing chain (SVC-051, cross-capability async); (2) fraud scoring of the transfer (SVC-013, cross-capability async); (3) SCA re-verification if the transfer exceeds the bank's high-value threshold (£50,000 equivalent). SVC-010 waits for TransferSanctionsScreened (EVT-051) and TransferFraudScored (EVT-052) before proceeding. Fail-closed: if either check is not received within 30 seconds, the transfer is blocked pending manual review.
channel: No customer-facing interaction — portal shows 'Compliance checks in progress'
persona_actions: Customer waits; portal displays progress indicator with estimated completion time
If SCA re-verification required for high-value transfer: customer completes second SCA step
system_actions: EVT-049 (and EVT-050 for cross-currency) triggers SVC-051 to screen: beneficiary name + IBAN + BIC; all correspondent banks in the routing chain
SVC-051 runs OFSI/UN/EU/OFAC sanctions screens concurrently for all entities; publishes TransferSanctionsScreened (EVT-051) with outcome (clear | hit | error) per entity
EVT-049 triggers SVC-013 to score the transfer for fraud (ML model trained on corporate wire patterns); publishes TransferFraudScored (EVT-052) with risk_score and risk_level
SVC-010 waits for both EVT-051 and EVT-052; applies correlation map keyed on transfer_id
If EVT-051.outcome = hit: SVC-010 sets InternationalTransfer.status = sanctions_blocked; publishes TransferFailed (EVT-057); MLRO alert raised
If EVT-052.risk_level = block: SVC-010 sets InternationalTransfer.status = fraud_blocked; publishes TransferFailed (EVT-057)
Both clear: SVC-010 sets InternationalTransfer.status = compliance_cleared; continues to PH-032
phases.exit_condition: Both EVT-051 and EVT-052 received with clear/non-block outcomes; InternationalTransfer.status = compliance_cleared; OR terminal TransferFailed (EVT-057) published

phases.name: SWIFT Message Assembly
phases.description: SVC-010 assembles the SWIFT payment message and determines the correspondent routing chain. For corporate international payments in 2026, SWIFT CBPR+ ISO 20022 (pacs.008 MX message) is mandatory — MT103 format is no longer accepted for new cross-border SWIFT traffic (MT coexistence period ended 22 November 2025). SVC-010 creates a SWIFTMessage record (ENT-029) and a CorrespondentRouting record (ENT-028). A SWIFT gpi UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference) is assigned at this stage. InternationalTransfer.status is set to message_assembled.
system_actions: SVC-010 determines the correspondent banking chain for the beneficiary BIC using the bank's correspondent routing table
SVC-010 creates CorrespondentRouting (ENT-028): routing_id, transfer_id, correspondent_chain[], nostro_account, charges_type
SVC-010 generates SWIFT gpi UETR (UUID v4) — immutable unique end-to-end reference; stored on InternationalTransfer.gpi_uetr

SVC-010 assembles SWIFT pacs.008 ISO 20022 MX message (mandatory post CBPR+ cutover November 2025); LEI included for corporate originator (GOV-003-R03); purpose code populated from transfer.purpose_code; structured beneficiary address required (GOV-003-R03)
SVC-010 creates SWIFTMessage (ENT-029): message_id, transfer_id, message_type = pacs008, raw_payload_ref
SVC-010 updates InternationalTransfer.status = message_assembled; sets InternationalTransfer.swift_reference
SVC-010 publishes TransferCleared (EVT-053) — signals that the transfer is ready for execution
phases.exit_condition: SWIFTMessage and CorrespondentRouting created; UETR assigned; EVT-053 (TransferCleared) published
nfr_references: UETR globally unique per SWIFT scheme rules

phases.name: Nostro/Correspondent Processing
phases.description: SVC-010 submits the assembled SWIFT message to the SWIFT network via the bank's SWIFT Alliance Access (or SAA Cloud) connectivity. The message is routed through the correspondent chain to the beneficiary bank. SVC-010 debits the bank's nostro account at the correspondent bank. An async event (AccountDebited) is published to SVC-005 (CAP-002) to debit the originating BusinessAccount. SVC-010 updates SWIFTMessage.sent_timestamp and sets InternationalTransfer.status = in_transit. On receipt of correspondent acknowledgement, EVT-055 (CorrespondentAcknowledged) is published.
channel: No customer-facing interaction — portal shows 'Transfer in progress'
persona_actions: Customer may monitor transfer status via portal tracker or SWIFT gpi tracker link
system_actions: SVC-010 consumes EVT-053 (TransferCleared); submits pacs.008 to SWIFT network via SWIFT Alliance Access (SAA Cloud)
SVC-010 updates SWIFTMessage.sent_timestamp; sets InternationalTransfer.status = in_transit
SVC-010 publishes SWIFTMessageSent (EVT-054)
SVC-010 publishes cross-capability async event to SVC-005 (CAP-002) requesting account debit for gbp_equivalent amount from the originating BusinessAccount
SVC-005
First correspondent bank in the chain receives the pacs.008; processes and forwards
On SWIFT gpi confirmation of correspondent acknowledgement: SVC-010 receives ACK; updates SWIFTMessage.ack_timestamp
SVC-010 publishes CorrespondentAcknowledged (EVT-055) with gpi_uetr and accepting_correspondent_bic
phases.exit_condition: EVT-054 (SWIFTMessageSent) published; EVT-055 (CorrespondentAcknowledged) received; BusinessAccount debited
nfr_references: Correspondent ACK SLA per SWIFT gpi rules (typically < 30 minutes for first hop)

phases.name: Confirmation & Tracking
phases.description: SVC-010 receives SWIFT gpi tracker updates as the payment progresses through the correspondent chain to the beneficiary bank. When the final credit is confirmed at the beneficiary bank (gpi status = ACCC — AcceptedCreditSettlementCompleted), SVC-010 updates InternationalTransfer.status = completed and publishes TransferCompleted (EVT-056). The customer receives a transfer completion notification. The SWIFT gpi UETR is shown in the portal tracker for end-to-end visibility.
persona_actions: View real-time transfer status in the portal tracker (status updates pushed as gpi tracker events are received)
Receive push notification and email confirmation when TransferCompleted (EVT-056) is published
Download transfer confirmation PDF (includes UETR, SWIFT reference, correspondent chain, execution timestamp)
system_actions: SVC-010 subscribes to SWIFT gpi tracker webhooks for the transfer's UETR
On each gpi status update: SVC-010 updates InternationalTransfer.status accordingly (in_transit → processing_at_correspondent → credit_confirmed)
On gpi final status ACCC: SVC-010 sets InternationalTransfer.status = completed
SVC-010 publishes TransferCompleted (EVT-056) with transfer_id, gpi_uetr, completed_at
SVC-053 (Notification Service) consumes EVT-056; dispatches push notification and email confirmation to PER-002
SVC-103 (Audit & Logging) creates immutable audit log entry
SVC-111 (WORM Compliance Store) archives transfer record per FATF travel rule retention obligations
phases.exit_condition: TransferCompleted (EVT-056) published; customer notified; audit trail archived
nfr_references: gpi tracker update latency < 60 seconds per hop

happy_path.description: PER-002 initiates a cross-currency international wire via the corporate portal. FX quote is obtained and accepted. Sanctions screening and fraud scoring return clear. SWIFT pacs.008 message is assembled with UETR. Message is submitted to SWIFT; correspondent bank acknowledges. BusinessAccount is debited. gpi tracker confirms credit at beneficiary bank. Customer receives completion notification. Total elapsed time: typically 30 minutes to 4 hours depending on correspondent chain and currency.

timing_breakdown.total_customer_to_beneficiary_credit: Same business day for major corridors (GBP/USD, GBP/EUR) with early cutoff submission

alternative_paths.name: GBP International Transfer (No FX Conversion)
alternative_paths.description: PER-002 initiates a GBP-denominated transfer to a beneficiary IBAN/BIC. No FX conversion is required. PH-030 is skipped. The transfer proceeds directly from PH-029 to PH-031. InternationalTransfer.fx_rate = 1.0000; gbp_equivalent = amount. A SWIFT pacs.008 is still assembled for the GBP-denominated cross-border instruction.

alternative_paths.name: Dual Authorisation for High-Value Transfer
alternative_paths.description: Transfer amount exceeds BusinessAccount.payment_approval_threshold. First authorised user initiates the transfer (reaches PH-029 exit with status = pending_second_authorisation). A second authorised user reviews and approves via the corporate portal. On second approval, SCA is completed by the second user. Transfer proceeds to PH-030/PH-031.

exception_paths.name: Sanctions Block
exception_paths.description: SVC-051 returns a sanctions match on the beneficiary, beneficiary BIC, or any correspondent bank in the chain. SVC-010 publishes TransferFailed (EVT-057) with reason = sanctions_block. InternationalTransfer.status = sanctions_blocked. MLRO is alerted. Customer sees a generic decline message — the tipping-off prohibition (GOV-005-R02, POCA 2002 s333A) prohibits disclosing the specific sanctions match. OFSI notification required within 14 days if a designated person is confirmed.
exception_paths.customer_message: Generic: 'We are unable to process this transfer. Please contact your Relationship Manager.'
exception_paths.internal_action: MLRO alert; OFSI notification within 14 days if designated person confirmed; transfer retained in sanctions_blocked status for audit

exception_paths.name: Fraud Block
exception_paths.description: SVC-013 fraud score for the transfer exceeds the block threshold (corporate wire fraud model). SVC-010 publishes TransferFailed (EVT-057) with reason = fraud_block. InternationalTransfer.status = fraud_blocked. Fraud Analyst (PER-054) is alerted for investigation. Customer sees a generic security decline message with contact information.
exception_paths.customer_message: 'This transfer has been blocked for security reasons. Please contact your Relationship Manager or call [fraud line].'
exception_paths.internal_action: PER-054 (Fraud Analyst) case created; RM (PER-050) notified

exception_paths.name: Correspondent Rejection
exception_paths.description: A correspondent bank in the chain rejects the pacs.008 message (e.g. invalid beneficiary account, AML block at correspondent). SVC-010 receives a SWIFT negative acknowledgement (pacs.002 RJCT). SVC-010 publishes TransferFailed (EVT-057) with reason = correspondent_rejection and the ISO 20022 reason code. InternationalTransfer.status = failed. The account debit is reversed (or not applied if the rejection arrives before debit confirmation). Customer is notified with the reason code and advised to re-initiate with corrected beneficiary details.
exception_paths.trigger: SWIFT pacs.002 rejection received from first correspondent or beneficiary bank
exception_paths.customer_message: 'Your transfer was rejected by the receiving bank. Reason: [standardised reason text]. No funds have been debited. Please check beneficiary details and try again.'
exception_paths.internal_action: Payment Operations team alerted; debit reversal instruction sent to SVC-005 if debit had been applied

exception_paths.name: FX Quote Lapse Without Acceptance
exception_paths.description: The firm FX quote (FXQuotation) lapses before PER-002 accepts it (validity_seconds exceeded). SVC-010 marks FXQuotation.status = lapsed and automatically re-quotes. If the customer declines the refreshed rate, the transfer is abandoned and InternationalTransfer.status = cancelled.
exception_paths.customer_message: 'Your FX rate has expired. A new rate has been calculated. Please review and confirm to proceed.'
exception_paths.internal_action: SVC-010 re-invokes FX pricing engine; publishes new FXQuoteProvided (EVT-050) with refreshed FXQuotation

design_decisions.decision: International Payments is a promoted sub-capability (CAP-003.04) with its own service SVC-010. SVC-010 may call SVC-009 (Domestic Payments) directly as a same-capability (CAP-003) synchronous call for the nostro-leg settlement. Cross-capability calls to SVC-005, SVC-051, and SVC-013 are async events only.
design_decisions.rationale: CAP-003.04 met all four promotion criteria (see capability definition). SVC-010 is introduced as a new service to own the international payment lifecycle: ENT-026 (InternationalTransfer), ENT-027 (FXQuotation), ENT-028 (CorrespondentRouting), ENT-029 (SWIFTMessage). Same-capability direct calls to SVC-009 are permitted per the bank's architectural principles. Cross-capability calls (account debit at SVC-005/CAP-002; sanctions at SVC-051/CAP-005; fraud at SVC-013/CAP-004) must be async events.

design_decisions.decision: SWIFT pacs.008 (ISO 20022 MX) is the sole message format. MT103 is not supported.
design_decisions.rationale: SWIFT CBPR+ MT coexistence period ended 22 November 2025. ISO 20022 MX messages are mandatory for all in-scope cross-border SWIFT traffic. Building MT103 support for new journeys would require dual-format maintenance with no business benefit and active compliance risk.

design_decisions.decision: Sanctions screening covers not only the beneficiary but all correspondent banks in the routing chain (beneficiary BIC and each intermediate BIC in correspondent_chain[]). This is performed before message submission, not after.
design_decisions.rationale: OFSI and OFAC require sanctions screening through the full payment chain, not just the direct counterparty. Correspondent bank screening at message assembly time (PH-031) prevents in-flight payments reaching a sanctioned correspondent — fail-closed before funds leave the bank.

design_decisions.decision: The SWIFT gpi UETR is assigned in PH-032 (message assembly) rather than at initiation (PH-029).
design_decisions.rationale: The UETR is a scheme-level identifier that must accompany the SWIFT message. Assigning it at initiation would require carrying a UETR through compliance checks before knowing whether the payment will proceed. Assigning at assembly is the correct SWIFT gpi architecture — the UETR is generated immediately before submission.
